## Natural history notes

A medium-sized stink bug characterized by its shield-shaped body, mottled brown coloration, pale edging or lines along the body, and long segmented antennae. In Florida, it is found in fields, gardens, roadsides, forest edges, agricultural areas, and other open or semi-open habitats with grasses, shrubs, and herbaceous plants. It feeds by piercing plant tissues and sucking sap from seeds, fruits, stems, and developing plant parts, while also serving as prey for spiders, birds, assassin bugs, and parasitoid wasps.
